records.source: וּלְאַחְאָ֛ב שִׁבְעִ֥ים בָּנִ֖ים בְּשֹׁמְר֑וֹן וַיִּכְתֹּב֩ יֵה֨וּא סְפָרִ֜ים וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח שֹׁמְר֗וֹן אֶל־שָׂרֵ֤י יִזְרְעֶאל֙ הַזְּקֵנִ֔ים וְאֶל־הָאֹמְנִ֥ים אַחְאָ֖ב לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And to Ahab [were] seventy sons in Samaria; and wrote Jehu letters and sent [them to] Samaria to [the] princes of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab, saying,
pieces: There were seventy sons of Ahab in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them there, to the officials of Jezreel, the elders, and those who were guardians of Ahab's sons. The letters said:

L.1: And Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. And Jehu wrote letters and sent [them to] Samaria, to the princes of Jezreel, the elders, and to the guardians of Ahab, saying,

R.1: Ahab had seventy sons living in the city of Samaria. So Jehu wrote letters and sent them to Samaria. He sent them to the leaders of Jezreel, to the elders, and to the men who were bringing up Ahab's sons. This is what he wrote:

decisions.choice: seventy sons: Ahab's male descendants, sons and grandsons
decisions.reason: "Sons" here covers the royal line as a whole: verse 3 speaks of "your master's sons" in a way that includes the sons of Joram, Ahab's son, who had just been killed (9:24). Seventy is a round number for a large royal family, as with Gideon's seventy sons (Judges 8:30; 9:5).

decisions.choice: the princes of Jezreel: the leading men of the royal court, now in Samaria
decisions.reason: The letters go to Samaria, yet the officials are called "of Jezreel". Jezreel was Ahab's second royal city (1 Kings 21:1), and these may be court officials who belonged to the Jezreel palace but were in Samaria. Some ancient translations, the Greek among them, read "the officials of the city" or "of Samaria" instead, a small change in the Hebrew. The Hebrew as it stands is followed.

decisions.choice: the guardians of Ahab: those who brought up Ahab's sons
decisions.reason: The word names the men who raised and protected royal children (Numbers 11:12; Isaiah 49:23). Verse 6 says the king's sons were with the great men of the city who were bringing them up. "Of Ahab" is short for "of Ahab's sons"; some ancient translations add "sons".

decisions.choice: Samaria: the capital of Israel
decisions.reason: Omri founded Samaria and made it his royal city (1 Kings 16:24). Jehu has seized the throne at Jezreel (9:14-37), but the capital, with its walls, troops and Ahab's heirs, is still in the hands of Ahab's officials.

decisions.choice: those who were guardians of Ahab's sons (Balanced); the men who were bringing up Ahab's sons (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose guardians they were (m3).

records.heading: The end of Ahab's family

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה כְּבֹ֨א הַסֵּ֤פֶר הַזֶּה֙ אֲלֵיכֶ֔ם וְאִתְּכֶ֖ם בְּנֵ֣י אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֑ם וְאִתְּכֶם֙ הָרֶ֣כֶב וְהַסּוּסִ֔ים וְעִ֥יר מִבְצָ֖ר וְהַנָּֽשֶׁק׃
records.gloss: And now, as comes the letter this to you, and with you [are the] sons of your master, and with you the chariotry and the horses and a city of fortification and the weapons,
pieces: "Now, the moment this letter reaches you, since you have your master's sons with you, along with chariots and horses, a fortified city and weapons,

L.2: "And now, as soon as this letter comes to you, since the sons of your master [are] with you, and with you [are] the chariots and the horses and a fortified city and the weapons,

R.2: "Your master's sons are there with you. You also have chariots and horses, a city with strong walls, and weapons. So as soon as this letter reaches you, do this.

decisions.choice: and now, as soon as this letter comes: the start of the letter's demand
decisions.reason: "And now" is the usual way a letter moves from greeting to business (5:6). The sentence runs on into verse 3, where the demand comes.

decisions.choice: chariots, horses, a fortified city, weapons: everything needed to resist
decisions.reason: Jehu lists the means of war that Samaria holds, as a challenge: if the officials want to fight for Ahab's house, they have all they need. The irony is that they have the means but not the will (verse 4).

decisions.choice: puts "as soon as this letter reaches you" after the list
decisions.reason: Readable states what the officials have first and then gives the command, so the long Hebrew sentence of verses 2-3 can be broken into short ones.

records.source: וּרְאִיתֶ֞ם הַטּ֤וֹב וְהַיָּשָׁר֙ מִבְּנֵ֣י אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֔ם וְשַׂמְתֶּ֖ם עַל־כִּסֵּ֣א אָבִ֑יו וְהִֽלָּחֲמ֖וּ עַל־בֵּ֥ית אֲדֹנֵיכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: and see the good and the upright from [the] sons of your master and set [him] on [the] throne of his father, and fight for [the] house of your master.
pieces: pick the best and most fitting of your master's sons, put him on his father's throne, and fight for the house of your master."

L.3: then see the best and most upright of the sons of your master, and set [him] on the throne of his father, and fight for the house of your master."

R.3: Choose the best and most able of your master's sons. Make him king in his father's place, and fight for your master's family."

decisions.choice: see: pick out, choose
decisions.reason: "See" here means to look over and choose, as in Genesis 22:8 and 1 Samuel 16:1, where it is used of choosing a king.

decisions.choice: the good and the upright: the fittest to be king
decisions.reason: The two words together mean the one best suited for the throne, in ability and character.

decisions.choice: fight for your master's house: a dare
decisions.reason: Jehu does not mean this as advice. He dares Ahab's officials to make a king and go to war, knowing they will not risk it after what happened to the two kings (verse 4).

decisions.choice: family
decisions.reason: Readable says "family" for "house" in the sense of a royal line, as at 1 Kings 16:3.

records.source: וַיִּֽרְאוּ֙ מְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֔ד וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ הִנֵּה֙ שְׁנֵ֣י הַמְּלָכִ֔ים לֹ֥א עָמְד֖וּ לְפָנָ֑יו וְאֵ֖יךְ נַעֲמֹ֥ד אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃
records.gloss: And they feared very very and said, look, [the] two the kings not stood before him, and how will stand we?
pieces: But they were terrified and said, "Look, the two kings could not stand against him. How can we?"

L.4: And they were exceedingly afraid and said, "Look, the two kings did not stand before him; and how will we stand?"

R.4: But the officials were badly frightened. They said, "Two kings could not stand up to Jehu. How can we?"

decisions.choice: very, very: the fear was extreme
decisions.reason: The word "very" is doubled for emphasis: they were utterly afraid.

decisions.choice: the two kings: Joram king of Israel and Ahaziah king of Judah
decisions.reason: Jehu had killed both of them a short time before (9:24, 27).

decisions.choice: stand before him: hold out against him
decisions.reason: To "stand before" an enemy is to resist him and survive (Joshua 10:8; Judges 2:14).

decisions.choice: Jehu
decisions.reason: Readable names Jehu for "him".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח אֲשֶׁר־עַל־הַבַּ֣יִת וַאֲשֶׁ֪ר עַל־הָעִ֟יר וְהַזְּקֵנִים֩ וְהָאֹמְנִ֨ים אֶל־יֵה֤וּא׀לֵאמֹר֙ עֲבָדֶ֣יךָ אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־תֹּאמַ֥ר אֵלֵ֖ינוּ נַעֲשֶׂ֑ה לֹֽא־נַמְלִ֣יךְ אִ֔ישׁ הַטּ֥וֹב בְּעֵינֶ֖יךָ עֲשֵֽׂה׃
records.gloss: And sent [the one] who [was] over the house and [the one] who [was] over the city and the elders and the guardians to Jehu, saying, your servants [are] we, and all that you say to us we will do; not we will make king anyone; the good in your eyes do.
pieces: So the palace steward, the governor of the city, the elders and the guardians sent word to Jehu: "We are your servants, and we will do everything you tell us. We will not make anyone king. Do whatever you think best."

L.5: And the [one] who [was] over the house, and the [one] who [was] over the city, and the elders, and the guardians sent to Jehu, saying, "We [are] your servants, and all that you say to us we will do. We will not make anyone king; do what [is] good in your eyes."

R.5: So the man in charge of the palace, the man in charge of the city, the elders and the guardians sent word back to Jehu: "We are your servants. We will do whatever you tell us. We will not make anyone king. Do what you think is best."

decisions.choice: the one over the house, the one over the city: the palace steward and the city governor
decisions.reason: "The one over the house" was the chief officer of the palace, a high post at court (1 Kings 4:6; 18:3). "The one over the city" was the official in charge of the capital (1 Kings 22:26).

decisions.choice: we are your servants: we submit to you
decisions.reason: Calling themselves his servants is a formal declaration of loyalty. The officials give up Ahab's house and accept Jehu as king.

decisions.choice: the good in your eyes: what you think best
decisions.reason: "In your eyes" means in your judgment (1 Samuel 1:23).

decisions.choice: your servants
decisions.reason: The officials speak of themselves politely as Jehu's servants, so "servants" is kept at every level, as in Genesis 18:3 and 1 Samuel 20.

decisions.choice: the palace steward, the governor of the city (Balanced); the man in charge of the palace, the man in charge of the city (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the two offices (m1).

records.source: וַיִּכְתֹּ֣ב אֲלֵיהֶם֩ סֵ֨פֶר׀שֵׁנִ֜ית לֵאמֹ֗ר אִם־לִ֨י אַתֶּ֜ם וּלְקֹלִ֣י׀אַתֶּ֣ם שֹׁמְעִ֗ים קְחוּ֙ אֶת־רָאשֵׁי֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֔ם וּבֹ֧אוּ אֵלַ֛י כָּעֵ֥ת מָחָ֖ר יִזְרְעֶ֑אלָה וּבְנֵ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ אֶת־גְּדֹלֵ֥י הָעִ֖יר מְגַדְּלִ֥ים אוֹתָֽם׃
records.gloss: And he wrote to them a letter second, saying, if mine [are] you and to my voice you [are] listening, take [the] heads of [the] men of [the] sons of your master and come to me at [the] time tomorrow to Jezreel. And [the] sons of the king, seventy man, [were] with [the] great [men] of the city, bringing up them.
pieces: Then he wrote them a second letter: "If you are on my side and will obey me, take the heads of the men, your master's sons, and be with me in Jezreel by this time tomorrow." Now the king's sons, seventy of them, were with the leading men of the city, who were bringing them up.

L.6: And he wrote to them a second letter, saying, "If you [are] mine, and you [are] listening to my voice, take the heads of the men, the sons of your master, and come to me at this time tomorrow to Jezreel." And the sons of the king, seventy persons, [were] with the great [men] of the city, who were bringing them up.

R.6: Then Jehu wrote them a second letter. It said, "If you are on my side and will do what I say, cut off the heads of your master's sons. Bring them to me at Jezreel by this time tomorrow." The seventy sons of the king were being brought up by the leading men of the city.

decisions.choice: if you are mine: if you are on my side
decisions.reason: "To be someone's" is to belong to his party (Joshua 5:13; 1 Kings 20:4). Jehu takes them at their word (verse 5).

decisions.choice: listening to my voice: obeying me
decisions.reason: To listen to someone's voice is the ordinary Hebrew way of saying to obey him.

decisions.choice: the heads of the men: both "the leaders" and the heads cut off
alternatives: the leaders of your master's sons
decisions.reason: "Heads" can mean the chief men of a group or the heads of their bodies. The officials could have taken Jehu to mean "bring the leading men among your master's sons". They understood it as a command to kill them (verse 7), and the double sense let Jehu later say he had not ordered it (verse 9).

decisions.choice: seventy man: seventy persons
decisions.reason: "Man" after a number counts individuals; the sons were probably of many ages, some still boys.

decisions.choice: the king's sons were with the great men: a note explaining the situation
decisions.reason: The last sentence steps out of the letter to tell where the sons were. The guardians of verse 1 were the city's great men.

decisions.choice: cut off the heads
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense the officials acted on (verse 7). The play on "heads" (m3) cannot be kept in plain words, and the note gives the other reading.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כְּבֹ֤א הַסֵּ֨פֶר֙ אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם וַיִּקְחוּ֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיִּשְׁחֲט֖וּ שִׁבְעִ֣ים אִ֑ישׁ וַיָּשִׂ֤ימוּ אֶת־רָֽאשֵׁיהֶם֙ בַּדּוּדִ֔ים וַיִּשְׁלְח֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו יִזְרְעֶֽאלָה׃
records.gloss: And it was, as came the letter to them, and they took the sons of the king and slaughtered seventy man, and put their heads in baskets and sent [them] to him to Jezreel.
pieces: When the letter came to them, they took the king's sons, seventy men, and slaughtered them. Then they put the heads in baskets and sent them to Jehu in Jezreel.

L.7: And it happened, as soon as the letter came to them, that they took the sons of the king and slaughtered [them], seventy persons, and put their heads in baskets and sent [them] to him at Jezreel.

R.7: When the letter came, the officials took the seventy sons of the king and killed every one of them. They packed the heads into baskets and had them taken to Jehu at Jezreel.

decisions.choice: slaughtered: killed as animals are killed
decisions.reason: The verb is used for slaughtering animals, for food or for sacrifice. Used of people it stresses the cold and wholesale killing (verse 14; 1 Kings 18:40).

decisions.choice: baskets: containers for carrying
decisions.reason: The word names a basket or a pot (Jeremiah 24:2; 1 Samuel 2:14). Here they are baskets for carrying the heads.

decisions.choice: the officials themselves kill the king's sons
decisions.reason: The guardians who should have protected Ahab's heirs kill them on Jehu's word. The judgment spoken against Ahab's house (1 Kings 21:21-24) is carried out by its own servants.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א הַמַּלְאָךְ֙ וַיַּגֶּד־ל֣וֹ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֵבִ֖יאוּ רָאשֵׁ֣י בְנֵֽי־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שִׂ֣ימוּ אֹתָ֞ם שְׁנֵ֧י צִבֻּרִ֛ים פֶּ֥תַח הַשַּׁ֖עַר עַד־הַבֹּֽקֶר׃
records.gloss: And came the messenger and told him, saying, they have brought [the] heads of [the] sons of the king. And he said, put them [in] two heaps [at the] entrance of the gate until the morning.
pieces: The messenger came and reported to Jehu, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." Jehu said, "Pile them in two heaps at the entrance of the city gate until morning."

L.8: And the messenger came and told him, saying, "They have brought the heads of the sons of the king." And he said, "Put them [in] two heaps at the entrance of the gate until the morning."

R.8: A messenger came and told Jehu, "They have brought the heads of the king's sons." Jehu said, "Pile them in two heaps by the city gate. Leave them there until morning."

decisions.choice: the entrance of the gate: the public place of the city
decisions.reason: The city gate was where people met, traded and held court. Heads piled there would be seen by all who came in and out of Jezreel. Assyrian kings of the time also piled the heads of enemies at city gates as a warning.

decisions.choice: heaps: piles
decisions.reason: The word is used only here in the Bible. It comes from a root meaning to heap up (Genesis 41:35, of grain).

decisions.choice: city gate
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "city" gate, since the gate of Jezreel is meant.

records.source: וַיְהִ֤י בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ וַיֵּצֵ֣א וַֽיַּעֲמֹ֔ד וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֶל־כָּל־הָעָ֔ם צַדִּקִ֖ים אַתֶּ֑ם הִנֵּ֨ה אֲנִ֜י קָשַׁ֤רְתִּי עַל־אֲדֹנִי֙ וָאֶהְרְגֵ֔הוּ וּמִ֥י הִכָּ֖ה אֶת־כָּל־אֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And it was in the morning, and he went out and stood and said to all the people, righteous [are] you; look, I conspired against my master and killed him, but who struck all these?
pieces: In the morning he went out, stood there and said to all the people, "You are innocent. It was I who plotted against my master and killed him. But who struck down all these?

L.9: And it happened in the morning that he went out and stood, and said to all the people, "You [are] righteous. Look, I conspired against my master and killed him; but who struck down all these?

R.9: In the morning Jehu went out and stood in front of all the people. He said, "You have done nothing wrong. I am the one who plotted against my master and killed him. But who killed all these?

decisions.choice: righteous: innocent, not to blame
decisions.reason: The word here has its legal sense: in the right, guiltless (Exodus 23:7; Deuteronomy 25:1). Jehu tells the people they bear no guilt for what has happened.

decisions.choice: who struck down all these?: Jehu shifts the blame
decisions.reason: Jehu admits killing Joram, but points to the heads and implies that others, the leaders of Samaria, killed Ahab's sons. He hides that they did it at his command (verse 6). His question also leads to his claim in verse 10 that the LORD himself is behind it all.

decisions.choice: conspired: plotted, formed a secret plan against
decisions.reason: The verb means to bind together, and so to plot. It is the word used for Jehu's plot at 9:14.

decisions.choice: You have done nothing wrong
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "righteous" means here (m1).

records.source: דְּע֣וּ אֵפ֗וֹא כִּי֩ לֹ֨א יִפֹּ֜ל מִדְּבַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אַ֔רְצָה אֲשֶׁר־דִּבֶּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה עַל־בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב וַיהוָ֣ה עָשָׂ֔ה אֵ֚ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר דִּבֶּ֔ר בְּיַ֖ד עַבְדּ֥וֹ אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: Know then that not will fall of [the] word of Yahweh to [the] ground which spoke Yahweh concerning [the] house of Ahab; and Yahweh has done what he spoke by [the] hand of his servant Elijah.
pieces: Know, then, that not one word that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke against the house of Ahab will fail. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Elijah."

L.10: Know then that nothing will fall to the ground of the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke concerning the house of Ahab, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke by the hand of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} slave Elijah."

R.10: So you can be sure that everything {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said against Ahab's family will happen. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has done what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do through {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant Elijah."

decisions.choice: not fall to the ground: not fail, not go unfulfilled
decisions.reason: A word that falls to the ground is one that comes to nothing (Joshua 21:45; 1 Samuel 3:19). Jehu says that every part of Yahweh's word will come true.

decisions.choice: what he spoke through his servant Elijah: the word against Ahab's house
decisions.reason: Elijah had told Ahab that Yahweh would cut off every male of his family and make his house like the houses of Jeroboam and Baasha (1 Kings 21:21-24). Jehu presents the killings as the fulfillment of that word (9:25-26, 36-37).

decisions.choice: by the hand of: through
decisions.reason: "By the hand of" names the one through whom a message is given (1 Kings 16:7).

decisions.choice: his servant Elijah: the prophet as Yahweh's servant
decisions.reason: Prophets are called Yahweh's servants (1 Kings 14:18; 18:36), because they belong to him and do his work.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "slave" for this word, as with Moses and David, and Balanced and Readable say "servant" (see m4).

records.source: וַיַּ֣ךְ יֵה֗וּא אֵ֣ת כָּל־הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֤ים לְבֵית־אַחְאָב֙ בְּיִזְרְעֶ֔אל וְכָל־גְּדֹלָ֖יו וּמְיֻדָּעָ֣יו וְכֹהֲנָ֑יו עַד־בִּלְתִּ֥י הִשְׁאִֽיר־ל֖וֹ שָׂרִֽיד׃
records.gloss: And struck Jehu all the remaining of [the] house of Ahab in Jezreel and all his great [men] and his acquaintances and his priests, until not he left to him a survivor.
pieces: So Jehu struck down everyone who was left of Ahab's house in Jezreel, along with all his leading men, his close friends and his priests, until he left him no survivor.

L.11: And Jehu struck down all who remained of the house of Ahab in Jezreel, and all his great [men], and his close friends, and his priests, until he left him no survivor.

R.11: Then Jehu killed everyone in Jezreel who was left from Ahab's family. He also killed all of Ahab's leading men, his close friends and his priests. He did not leave a single one of them alive.

decisions.choice: acquaintances: close friends, trusted advisers
decisions.reason: The word means "those known" to someone, his intimate circle (Psalm 31:12; 55:14). At court they were the king's confidants.

decisions.choice: his priests: the priests who served Ahab's house
decisions.reason: These may have been priests of Baal attached to the royal family, or the priests of the court who served the king's own shrines. The text does not say which.

decisions.choice: no survivor: Jehu goes beyond the family
decisions.reason: The word against Ahab named his male descendants (1 Kings 21:21). Jehu also kills Ahab's officials, friends and priests, clearing away everyone who might support a rival. Later the prophet Hosea speaks of judgment on Jehu's house for "the blood of Jezreel" (Hosea 1:4).

decisions.choice: did not leave a single one of them alive
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "no survivor" means and makes "him" refer to Ahab's whole circle.

records.source: וַיָּ֨קָם֙ וַיָּבֹ֔א וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ שֹׁמְר֑וֹן ה֛וּא בֵּֽית־עֵ֥קֶד הָרֹעִ֖ים בַּדָּֽרֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And he arose and came and went [to] Samaria; he [was at] Beth-eked of the Shepherds on the way,
pieces: Then Jehu set out and went to Samaria. On the way, when he was at Beth-eked of the Shepherds,

L.12: And he arose and came and went [to] Samaria. He [was at] Beth-eked of the Shepherds on the way,

R.12: Then Jehu set out for Samaria. On the way he stopped at a place called Beth-eked of the Shepherds.

decisions.choice: Beth-eked of the Shepherds: a place between Jezreel and Samaria
decisions.reason: The name means "house of binding of the shepherds", perhaps a place where shepherds tied up their sheep for shearing. Its site is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: he was at Beth-eked on the way: setting the scene for verse 13
decisions.reason: The Hebrew sentence runs on into the next verse, where the meeting at Beth-eked is told.

decisions.choice: arose and came and went: he set out
decisions.reason: The three verbs together mean simply that he got up and made the journey. The Greek translation reads them differently, but the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: a place called
decisions.reason: Readable tells the reader that Beth-eked is a place name, and closes the sentence here instead of running it into verse 13.

records.source: וְיֵה֗וּא מָצָא֙ אֶת־אֲחֵי֙ אֲחַזְיָ֣הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מִ֣י אַתֶּ֑ם וַיֹּאמְר֗וּ אֲחֵ֤י אֲחַזְיָ֨הוּ֙ אֲנַ֔חְנוּ וַנֵּ֛רֶד לִשְׁל֥וֹם בְּנֵֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וּבְנֵ֥י הַגְּבִירָֽה׃
records.gloss: and Jehu found [the] brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah and said, who [are] you? And they said, [the] brothers of Ahaziah [are] we, and we have come down for [the] peace of [the] sons of the king and [the] sons of the queen mother.
pieces: Jehu met relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah. "Who are you?" he asked. They answered, "We are Ahaziah's relatives. We have come down to greet the king's sons and the queen mother's sons."

L.13: and Jehu found the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah, and he said, "Who [are] you?" And they said, "We [are] the brothers of Ahaziah, and we have come down to greet the sons of the king and the sons of the queen mother."

R.13: There Jehu met some relatives of Ahaziah king of Judah. He asked them, "Who are you?" They answered, "We are relatives of King Ahaziah. We have come to visit the sons of King Joram and of the queen mother."

decisions.choice: brothers: relatives, members of the royal family
decisions.reason: "Brothers" can mean any male relatives. Ahaziah's own brothers had been killed by raiders earlier (2 Chronicles 21:17); 2 Chronicles 22:8 calls these men "the sons of Ahaziah's brothers", that is, his nephews and kinsmen.

decisions.choice: for the peace of: to greet, to ask after the welfare of
decisions.reason: To come "for the peace" of someone is to pay a friendly visit and ask how they are (1 Samuel 25:5).

decisions.choice: the queen mother: Jezebel
decisions.reason: The word means "great lady" and names the king's mother, who held a place of honor at court (1 Kings 15:13). In Israel this was Jezebel, Joram's mother. The visitors had not heard that Joram, Ahaziah and Jezebel were already dead (9:24-37). The kings of Judah were related to Ahab's house: Ahaziah's mother Athaliah was Ahab's daughter (8:18, 26).

decisions.choice: come down: traveled from Judah
decisions.reason: Jerusalem lies high in the hills, so the journey north was spoken of as going down.

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "relatives" for "brothers", since the men were Ahaziah's kinsmen (m1).

decisions.choice: the sons of King Joram
decisions.reason: Readable names the king meant, Joram of Israel, so readers do not confuse him with Ahaziah.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ תִּפְשׂ֣וּם חַיִּ֔ים וַֽיִּתְפְּשׂ֖וּם חַיִּ֑ים וַֽיִּשְׁחָט֞וּם אֶל־בּ֣וֹר בֵּֽית־עֵ֗קֶד אַרְבָּעִ֤ים וּשְׁנַ֨יִם֙ אִ֔ישׁ וְלֹֽא־הִשְׁאִ֥יר אִ֖ישׁ מֵהֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And he said, seize them alive. And they seized them alive and slaughtered them at [the] pit of Beth-eked, forty and two man, and not he left a man of them.
pieces: Jehu said, "Take them alive!" So they took them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked, forty-two men. He did not spare a single one of them.

L.14: And he said, "Seize them alive." And they seized them alive and slaughtered them at the pit of Beth-eked, forty-two men, and he did not leave a man of them.

R.14: Jehu ordered, "Take them alive!" So his men captured them. Then they killed all forty-two of them beside the well at Beth-eked. Jehu did not let even one of them live.

decisions.choice: pit: a cistern or well
decisions.reason: The word names a pit dug to hold water. The bodies may have been thrown into it (Jeremiah 41:7, 9).

decisions.choice: forty-two men: the killing reaches the house of David
decisions.reason: These men were of the royal family of Judah. Jehu's purge goes beyond Ahab's house, and leaves David's line so weakened that Athaliah can try to destroy it soon after (11:1).

decisions.choice: well
decisions.reason: Readable says "well" for the water pit, a word young readers know.

records.source: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ מִשָּׁ֡ם וַיִּמְצָ֣א אֶת־יְהוֹנָדָב֩ בֶּן־רֵכָ֨ב לִקְרָאת֜וֹ וַֽיְבָרְכֵ֗הוּ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו הֲיֵ֧שׁ אֶת־לְבָבְךָ֣ יָשָׁ֗ר כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר לְבָבִי֙ עִם־לְבָבֶ֔ךָ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוֹנָדָ֥ב יֵ֛שׁ וָיֵ֖שׁ תְּנָ֣ה אֶת־יָדֶ֑ךָ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן יָד֔וֹ וַיַּעֲלֵ֥הוּ אֵלָ֖יו אֶל־הַמֶּרְכָּבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he went from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab [coming] to meet him, and he blessed him and said to him, is there your heart upright as my heart [is] with your heart? And said Jehonadab, there is. And there is, give your hand. And he gave his hand, and he made him go up to him into the chariot.
pieces: Leaving there, he came upon Jehonadab son of Rechab, who was on his way to meet him. Jehu greeted him and said to him, "Is your heart right with mine, as my heart is with yours?" Jehonadab replied, "It is." "If so," said Jehu, "give me your hand." He gave him his hand, and Jehu took him up into the chariot beside him.

L.15: And he went from there and found Jehonadab son of Rechab [coming] to meet him, and he greeted him and said to him, "Is your heart right, as my heart [is] with your heart?" And Jehonadab said, "It is." "If it is, give [me] your hand." And he gave his hand, and he took him up to himself into the chariot.

R.15: As Jehu went on from there, Jehonadab son of Rechab came out to meet him. Jehu greeted him and asked, "Are you loyal to me, as I am to you?" Jehonadab answered, "I am." Jehu said, "Then give me your hand." Jehonadab gave him his hand, and Jehu helped him up into the chariot with him.

decisions.choice: is your heart right, as my heart is with your heart?: are you loyal to me as I am to you?
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of will and purpose. A heart that is "right" or "straight" with another's is one that is loyal and sincere toward him. Jehu asks whether Jehonadab is wholly with him.

decisions.choice: Jehonadab son of Rechab: the founder of the Rechabites
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 35 tells of Jonadab son of Rechab, who commanded his descendants never to drink wine, build houses, sow seed or plant vineyards, but to live in tents. His family kept that rule for some 250 years. His name in Jeremiah is the shorter form of the same name. His support gave Jehu's cause the backing of a man known for strict loyalty to Yahweh.

decisions.choice: It is. If it is, give me your hand: Jehonadab answers, then Jehu speaks
alternatives: It is, it is! Give me your hand
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "there is, and there is" with no new speaker named. It is best read as Jehonadab's answer, "It is", followed by Jehu's reply, "If it is, give me your hand". The Greek translation adds "and Jehu said". It can also be read as Jehonadab's emphatic "It is, it is!", with Jehu's command following.

decisions.choice: give your hand: clasp hands in pledge
decisions.reason: Giving the hand was a sign of agreement and loyalty (Ezra 10:19; Ezekiel 17:18). Jehu then takes Jehonadab into his chariot as an honored ally.

decisions.choice: he blessed him: he greeted him
decisions.reason: "Bless" is used of a greeting, wishing someone well (4:29; 1 Samuel 13:10).

decisions.choice: said Jehu (Balanced); Jehu said (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jehu as the speaker of the last words, as the sense requires (m3).

decisions.choice: Are you loyal to me, as I am to you?
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what the picture of the heart means (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לְכָ֣ה אִתִּ֔י וּרְאֵ֖ה בְּקִנְאָתִ֣י לַיהוָ֑ה וַיַּרְכִּ֥בוּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּרִכְבּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he said, come with me and see my zeal for Yahweh; and they made him ride in his chariot.
pieces: He said, "Come with me and see how zealous I am for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." So they had him ride in Jehu's chariot.

L.16: And he said, "Come with me and see my zeal for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}." And they made him ride in his chariot.

R.16: Jehu said, "Come with me. See how much I care about {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s honor." So Jehonadab rode along in Jehu's chariot.

decisions.choice: zeal: burning devotion that will not tolerate a rival
decisions.reason: The word names a strong, jealous passion. It is used of Phinehas, who killed those who joined in the worship of Baal of Peor (Numbers 25:11, 13), and of Elijah (1 Kings 19:10, 14). Jehu claims the same zeal against the worship of Baal.

decisions.choice: they made him ride: Jehu's men, or Jehu himself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is plural, meaning Jehu's men seated Jehonadab in the chariot. The Greek translation and others have the singular, "he made him ride". The sense is the same.

decisions.choice: his chariot: Jehu's chariot
decisions.reason: "His" refers to Jehu, as verse 15 shows.

decisions.choice: Jehu's chariot
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jehu for "his" (m3).

decisions.choice: how much I care about the LORD's honor
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word "zeal" (m1).

records.source: וַיָּבֹא֙ שֹֽׁמְר֔וֹן וַ֠יַּךְ אֶת־כָּל־הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֧ים לְאַחְאָ֛ב בְּשֹׁמְר֖וֹן עַד־הִשְׁמִיד֑וֹ כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר דִּבֶּ֖ר אֶל־אֵלִיָּֽהוּ׃פ
records.gloss: And he came [to] Samaria and struck all the remaining of Ahab in Samaria until he destroyed him, according to [the] word of Yahweh which he spoke to Elijah.
pieces: When he came to Samaria, he struck down everyone who was left of Ahab's family in Samaria, until he had wiped them out, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said through Elijah.

L.17: And he came [to] Samaria and struck down all who remained of Ahab in Samaria, until he had destroyed him, according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} spoke to Elijah.

R.17: When Jehu reached Samaria, he killed everyone left there from Ahab's family. He wiped them all out, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told Elijah.

decisions.choice: until he destroyed him: until Ahab's house was wiped out
decisions.reason: "Him" stands for Ahab, meaning all that was left of his house.

decisions.choice: according to the word spoken to Elijah
decisions.reason: As in verse 10. Yahweh's word to Elijah about Ahab's house (1 Kings 21:21-24) is carried out in Samaria as it was in Jezreel.

decisions.choice: Ahab's family ... them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "family" and use "them" for the collective "him" (m1).

records.source: וַיִּקְבֹּ֤ץ יֵהוּא֙ אֶת־כָּל־הָעָ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֲלֵהֶ֔ם אַחְאָ֕ב עָבַ֥ד אֶת־הַבַּ֖עַל מְעָ֑ט יֵה֖וּא יַעַבְדֶ֥נּוּ הַרְבֵּֽה׃
records.gloss: And gathered Jehu all the people and said to them, Ahab served the Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.
pieces: Then Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, "Ahab served Baal a little. Jehu will serve him much more.

L.18: And Jehu gathered all the people and said to them, "Ahab served the Baal a little; Jehu will serve him much.

R.18: Then Jehu called all the people together. He said, "Ahab worshiped Baal a little. I, Jehu, will worship him much more.

decisions.choice: Ahab served Baal a little: a lie, and also an irony
decisions.reason: Ahab had built a temple and altar for Baal in Samaria (1 Kings 16:31-32). Jehu pretends that he will go even further, to deceive Baal's followers (verse 19). In a sense he speaks truly: he will "serve" Baal by destroying his worship.

decisions.choice: the Baal: the Canaanite storm god
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the article, "the Baal", as at 1 Kings 16:31-32: the god who was worshiped as giver of rain and fertility. Jezebel had made his worship the religion of the court.

decisions.choice: the Baal
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the article wherever the Hebrew has it, as at 1 Kings 16:31-32; Balanced and Readable say "Baal" throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: worshiped ... worship
decisions.reason: Readable says "worship" for "serve" when it is used of a god.

records.heading: Jehu destroys Baal worship

records.source: וְעַתָּ֣ה כָל־נְבִיאֵ֣י הַבַּ֡עַל כָּל־עֹבְדָ֣יו וְכָל־כֹּהֲנָיו֩ קִרְא֨וּ אֵלַ֜י אִ֣ישׁ אַל־יִפָּקֵ֗ד כִּי֩ זֶ֨בַח גָּד֥וֹל לִי֙ לַבַּ֔עַל כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־יִפָּקֵ֖ד לֹ֣א יִֽחְיֶ֑ה וְיֵהוּא֙ עָשָׂ֣ה בְעָקְבָּ֔ה לְמַ֥עַן הַאֲבִ֖יד אֶת־עֹבְדֵ֥י הַבָּֽעַל׃
records.gloss: And now, all [the] prophets of the Baal, all serving him, and all his priests, call to me; a man not let be missing, for a sacrifice great [is] to me for the Baal; anyone who is missing not will live. And Jehu acted with cunning, so as to destroy [the] serving of the Baal.
pieces: Now summon to me all the prophets of Baal, all his worshipers and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I am holding a great sacrifice for Baal. Anyone who is missing will not live." But Jehu was acting with cunning, so that he could destroy the worshipers of Baal.

L.19: And now, call to me all the prophets of the Baal, all who serve him, and all his priests. Let no one be missing, for I have a great sacrifice for the Baal. Whoever is missing will not live." But Jehu acted with cunning, in order to destroy those who serve the Baal.

R.19: So call all of Baal's prophets, worshipers and priests to come to me. Do not let anyone stay away, because I am going to offer a great sacrifice to Baal. Anyone who does not come will be put to death." But Jehu was tricking them. He planned to kill everyone who worshiped Baal.

decisions.choice: a great sacrifice: the sacrifice will be the worshipers themselves
decisions.reason: Jehu means one thing and they hear another. The great sacrifice he plans is the killing of Baal's worshipers, as Elijah killed the prophets of Baal (1 Kings 18:40). The verb for killing in war or judgment is used elsewhere as a picture of sacrifice (Isaiah 34:6; Jeremiah 46:10).

decisions.choice: cunning: deceit, trickery
decisions.reason: The word comes from the root of Jacob's name and means crooked, underhanded dealing (Genesis 27:36). The writer states openly that Jehu's zeal used a lie.

decisions.choice: those who serve him: Baal's worshipers
decisions.reason: The word means those who serve a god by worship. It is set against "the servants of Yahweh" in verse 23.

decisions.choice: worshipers (Balanced); worshiped (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "those who serve"; Balanced and Readable say "worshipers", which is what serving a god means here (m3). The same wording is kept through verse 23.

decisions.choice: no one
decisions.reason: "A man" here means any person, so "no one" is used at every level.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יֵה֗וּא קַדְּשׁ֧וּ עֲצָרָ֛ה לַבַּ֖עַל וַיִּקְרָֽאוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Jehu, consecrate an assembly for the Baal; and they proclaimed [it].
pieces: Jehu said, "Set apart a solemn assembly for Baal." So they announced it.

L.20: And Jehu said, "Consecrate a solemn assembly for the Baal." And they proclaimed [it].

R.20: Jehu said, "Call a holy festival for Baal." So they announced it.

decisions.choice: consecrate a solemn assembly: proclaim a holy festival
decisions.reason: The noun names a sacred gathering on which no work was done, used of Israel's own festivals (Leviticus 23:36; Deuteronomy 16:8; Joel 1:14). "Consecrate" means to set it apart as holy. Jehu gives Baal's festival all the outward forms of true worship.

decisions.choice: holy festival
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain phrase for the "solemn assembly".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יֵהוּא֙ בְּכָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ כָּל־עֹבְדֵ֣י הַבַּ֔עַל וְלֹֽא־נִשְׁאַ֥ר אִ֖ישׁ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לֹֽא־בָ֑א וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית הַבַּ֔עַל וַיִּמָּלֵ֥א בֵית־הַבַּ֖עַל פֶּ֥ה לָפֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And sent Jehu through all Israel, and came all [the] serving of the Baal, and not was left a man who not came; and they came [into the] house of the Baal, and was filled [the] house of the Baal mouth to mouth.
pieces: Jehu sent word through all Israel, and all the worshipers of Baal came. Not one was left who did not come. They went into the temple of Baal, and the temple of Baal was filled from one end to the other.

L.21: And Jehu sent through all Israel, and all who serve the Baal came, and there was not a man left who did not come. And they came into the house of the Baal, and the house of the Baal was filled from mouth to mouth.

R.21: Jehu sent messengers all over Israel. All the people who worshiped Baal came. Not one of them stayed away. They went into Baal's temple, and they filled it from wall to wall.

decisions.choice: the house of the Baal: Baal's temple in Samaria
decisions.reason: Ahab had built this temple in Samaria (1 Kings 16:32). "House" is the usual word for a temple, the god's dwelling.

decisions.choice: mouth to mouth: from one end to the other
decisions.reason: The "mouth" is an opening or edge, so "mouth to mouth" means from one side to the other, completely full (21:16, of blood filling Jerusalem).

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "temple" for the god's "house", as at 1 Kings 16:32.

records.source: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לַֽאֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־הַמֶּלְתָּחָ֔ה הוֹצֵ֣א לְב֔וּשׁ לְכֹ֖ל עֹבְדֵ֣י הַבָּ֑עַל וַיֹּצֵ֥א לָהֶ֖ם הַמַּלְבּֽוּשׁ׃
records.gloss: And he said to [the one] who [was] over the wardrobe, bring out clothing for all [the] serving of the Baal; and he brought out for them the clothing.
pieces: Jehu told the keeper of the wardrobe, "Bring out robes for every worshiper of Baal." And he brought robes out for them.

L.22: And he said to the [one] who [was] over the wardrobe, "Bring out clothing for all who serve the Baal." And he brought out the clothing for them.

R.22: Jehu said to the man in charge of the special clothes, "Bring out robes for everyone who worships Baal." So the man brought out robes for them.

decisions.choice: the wardrobe: the room where the temple's garments were kept
decisions.reason: The word is found only here in the Bible. From the context it is a store of clothing, probably the vestments worn by worshipers at Baal's festival.

decisions.choice: clothing: special robes for worship
decisions.reason: Worshipers were given festal garments for the rite. The robes also marked out every worshiper of Baal, so that no one else could be mistaken for them (verse 23).

decisions.choice: robes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "robes" for the garments worn at the festival (m2).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֥א יֵה֛וּא וִיהוֹנָדָ֥ב בֶּן־רֵכָ֖ב בֵּ֣ית הַבָּ֑עַל וַיֹּ֜אמֶר לְעֹבְדֵ֣י הַבַּ֗עַל חַפְּשׂ֤וּ וּרְאוּ֙ פֶּן־יֶשׁ־פֹּ֤ה עִמָּכֶם֙ מֵעַבְדֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה כִּ֛י אִם־עֹבְדֵ֥י הַבַּ֖עַל לְבַדָּֽם׃
records.gloss: And came Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab [into the] house of the Baal, and he said to [the] serving of the Baal, search and see lest there be here with you of [the] servants of Yahweh, but only [the] serving of the Baal by themselves.
pieces: Then Jehu went into the temple of Baal with Jehonadab son of Rechab. He said to the worshipers of Baal, "Search and make sure that none of the servants of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are here with you, but only the worshipers of Baal."

L.23: And Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab went into the house of the Baal, and he said to those who serve the Baal, "Search and see that there is not here with you any of the servants of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, but only those who serve the Baal by themselves."

R.23: Then Jehu and Jehonadab son of Rechab went into Baal's temple. Jehu said to the worshipers of Baal, "Look around and make sure that no one who worships {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is here with you. Only those who worship Baal may be here."

decisions.choice: the servants of Yahweh: those who worship Yahweh
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means Yahweh's worshipers in general, set against "those who serve Baal". Jehu wants no one loyal to Yahweh to die in the killing that follows.

decisions.choice: he said: Jehu said
decisions.reason: The speaker is Jehu, who is in command; Jehonadab is with him as a witness (verse 16).

decisions.choice: servants of the LORD
decisions.reason: Literal usually says "slave" for this word. Here it says "servants", because the phrase means worshipers and is set against "those who serve the Baal" in the same sentence (m1). The likeness in Hebrew between the two expressions is kept that way.

decisions.choice: no one who worships the LORD
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "servants of the LORD" means here (m1).

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֕אוּ לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת זְבָחִ֣ים וְעֹל֑וֹת וְיֵה֞וּא שָׂם־ל֤וֹ בַחוּץ֙ שְׁמֹנִ֣ים אִ֔ישׁ וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הָאִ֤ישׁ אֲשֶׁר־יִמָּלֵט֙ מִן־הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר אֲנִי֙ מֵבִ֣יא עַל־יְדֵיכֶ֔ם נַפְשׁ֖וֹ תַּ֥חַת נַפְשֽׁוֹ׃
records.gloss: And they came to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings; and Jehu had set for himself outside eighty man, and he said, the man who escapes from the men whom I [am] bringing into your hands, his life in place of his life.
pieces: The worshipers went in to make sacrifices and burnt offerings. Jehu had already posted eighty men outside and had warned them, "If any of the men I am bringing into your hands escapes, the one who let him go will pay with his life."

L.24: And they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Now Jehu had stationed for himself eighty men outside, and he had said, "The man who escapes from the men whom I am bringing into your hands, his life [will be] in place of his life."

R.24: Then they went in to offer sacrifices and burnt offerings. Jehu had already placed eighty soldiers outside. He had told them, "I am handing these people over to you. If anyone lets one of them get away, he will die in that person's place."

decisions.choice: sacrifices and burnt offerings: the full rite of a festival
decisions.reason: Sacrifices were partly eaten by the worshipers; burnt offerings were burned whole on the altar. The festival goes ahead as if it were real.

decisions.choice: his life for his life: the guard pays with his life for the one who escapes
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the man who escapes from the men I bring into your hands". It means: if any worshiper escapes, the guard who let him go will die in his place. The verb can also be read as "lets escape", which gives the same sense. Compare 1 Kings 20:39, "your life will be for his life".

decisions.choice: had stationed ... had said: done before the worshipers went in
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word order puts Jehu first, marking a step taken beforehand: the guards were already in place.

decisions.choice: bringing into your hands: putting in your power
decisions.reason: To give someone into another's hand is to put him under his power (Judges 6:1).

decisions.choice: will pay with his life (Balanced); will die in that person's place (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "his life for his life" means (m2).

decisions.choice: soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says "soldiers" for the eighty "men", since they were armed guards (verse 25).

records.source: וַיְהִ֞י כְּכַלֹּת֣וֹ׀לַעֲשׂ֣וֹת הָעֹלָ֗ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יֵ֠הוּא לָרָצִ֨ים וְלַשָּׁלִשִׁ֜ים בֹּ֤אוּ הַכּוּם֙ אִ֣ישׁ אַל־יֵצֵ֔א וַיַּכּ֖וּם לְפִי־חָ֑רֶב וַיַּשְׁלִ֗כוּ הָֽרָצִים֙ וְהַשָּׁ֣לִשִׁ֔ים וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ עַד־עִ֥יר בֵּית־הַבָּֽעַל׃
records.gloss: And it was, as he finished offering the burnt offering, and said Jehu to the runners and to the officers, go in, strike them; a man not let come out. And they struck them by [the] mouth of [the] sword, and threw [them] out the runners and the officers, and they went to [the] city of [the] house of the Baal.
pieces: The moment he had finished offering the burnt offering, Jehu ordered the guards and the officers, "Go in and kill them. Do not let anyone get out." So they killed them with the sword. The guards and the officers threw the bodies out and then went into the inner shrine of the temple of Baal.

L.25: And it happened, as soon as he had finished offering the burnt offering, that Jehu said to the runners and to the officers, "Go in, strike them down; let no one come out." And they struck them down with the edge of the sword, and the runners and the officers threw [them] out, and they went to the city of the house of the Baal.

R.25: As soon as the burnt offering had been offered, Jehu said to the guards and the officers, "Go in and kill them. Do not let anyone get away." So they went in and killed them all with their swords. The guards and the officers threw the bodies out. Then they went into the inner rooms of Baal's temple.

decisions.choice: as he finished: probably Jehu himself, who led the offering
decisions.reason: "He" most naturally refers to Jehu, who had come into the temple and, as king, presided at the sacrifice (verses 23-24). It may also mean the priest who made the offering. Either way the killing begins when the rite is complete.

decisions.choice: the runners and the officers: the royal guard and its captains
decisions.reason: The runners were the king's guard (1 Kings 14:27). The officers were the king's high-ranking soldiers; the word is linked with "three" and may first have named the third man in a chariot (9:25; 1 Kings 9:22).

decisions.choice: by the mouth of the sword: with the sword, without mercy
decisions.reason: The edge of a sword is called its "mouth", as if it devours. The phrase means killing in battle, sparing no one (Joshua 6:21).

decisions.choice: the city of the house of Baal: probably the inner shrine of the temple
alternatives: the citadel of the temple of Baal
the inner room of the temple of Baal
decisions.reason: "City" here is unusual. It may mean a walled inner area of the temple, the sanctuary itself, where the pillar of Baal stood (verses 26-27). Some think a similar Hebrew word for the inner room of a temple (1 Kings 6:5) stood here at first. Others take it as the fortified temple area as a whole.

decisions.choice: threw them out: the bodies
decisions.reason: The object is not stated. They threw the bodies outside the temple so that they could reach the inner shrine.

decisions.choice: guards
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable call the runners "guards", as at 1 Kings 14:27.

decisions.choice: inner shrine (Balanced); inner rooms (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the most likely sense of "city" here (m4).

decisions.choice: the burnt offering had been offered
decisions.reason: Readable leaves the one who offered unnamed, as the matter is not certain (m1).

records.source: וַיֹּצִ֛אוּ אֶת־מַצְּב֥וֹת בֵּית־הַבַּ֖עַל וַֽיִּשְׂרְפֽוּהָ׃
records.gloss: And they brought out [the] standing stones of [the] house of the Baal and burned it.
pieces: They brought out the standing stones of the temple of Baal and burned them.

L.26: And they brought out the standing stones of the house of the Baal and burned it.

R.26: They carried the pillars out of Baal's temple and burned them.

decisions.choice: standing stones: sacred pillars set up for worship
decisions.reason: A standing stone was an upright pillar set up as a sign of a god's presence. Israel was commanded to break down those of the Canaanites (Exodus 23:24; Deuteronomy 12:3).

decisions.choice: standing stones ... burned it: the number does not agree
alternatives: the pillar of the house of Baal
the Asherah pole of the house of Baal
decisions.reason: The noun is plural but "it" is singular. Some ancient translations read "the pillar" in the singular, and some think the object burned was a wooden post such as an Asherah pole, since stone does not burn. Pillars of wood, or stone pillars cracked by fire, are both possible. Verse 27 then speaks of the chief pillar of Baal, which was pulled down.

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" to agree with the plural noun; the note gives the singular (m2).

decisions.choice: pillars
decisions.reason: Readable says "pillars" without "stone" here, since they were burned and may have been made of wood (m2).

records.source: וַֽיִּתְּצ֔וּ אֵ֖ת מַצְּבַ֣ת הַבָּ֑עַל וַֽיִּתְּצוּ֙ אֶת־בֵּ֣ית הַבַּ֔עַל וַיְשִׂמֻ֥הוּ לְמֽוֹצָא֖וֹת עַד־הַיּֽוֹם׃
records.gloss: And they pulled down [the] standing stone of the Baal, and pulled down [the] house of the Baal, and made it into latrines until this day.
pieces: They demolished the standing stone of Baal and tore down the temple of Baal, and they made it a latrine, as it is to this day.

L.27: And they pulled down the standing stone of the Baal, and they pulled down the house of the Baal and made it into latrines to this day.

R.27: They broke down Baal's stone pillar and tore down Baal's temple. They turned the place into a public toilet, and it is still that way to this day.

decisions.choice: latrines: the reading marked to be read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants (ketiv) read a coarse word for "places of dung". The scribes marked a milder word, "places of going out", to be read aloud (qere), as a polite way of saying the same thing. Both name latrines.

decisions.choice: made it a latrine: the worst possible defiling of a holy place
decisions.reason: Turning Baal's temple into a latrine made sure it could never again be used for worship. It was a deliberate act of contempt.

decisions.choice: to this day: the writer's own day
decisions.reason: As at 2:22, the first time the phrase is used in 2 Kings, "to this day" means up to the time when the writer was composing the account.

decisions.choice: public toilet
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain modern words for "latrine".

records.source: וַיַּשְׁמֵ֥ד יֵה֛וּא אֶת־הַבַּ֖עַל מִיִּשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And destroyed Jehu the Baal from Israel.
pieces: So Jehu wiped out Baal worship from Israel.

L.28: And Jehu wiped out the Baal from Israel.

R.28: In this way Jehu got rid of the worship of Baal in Israel.

decisions.choice: destroyed Baal from Israel: wiped out the worship of Baal
decisions.reason: The verb means to destroy completely. "Baal" stands for his worship: his priests, prophets, worshipers, pillar and temple. The worship of Baal that Ahab and Jezebel had brought in (1 Kings 16:31-32) was ended in Israel, though it returned in Judah under Athaliah (11:18).

decisions.choice: Baal worship (Balanced); the worship of Baal (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that it was Baal's worship that Jehu destroyed (m1).

records.source: רַ֠ק חֲטָאֵ֞י יָרָבְעָ֤ם בֶּן־נְבָט֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶחֱטִ֣יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל לֹֽא־סָ֥ר יֵה֖וּא מֵאַֽחֲרֵיהֶ֑ם עֶגְלֵי֙ הַזָּהָ֔ב אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּֽית־אֵ֖ל וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּדָֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Only [the] sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat which he made sin Israel, not turned aside Jehu from after them, [the] calves of the gold which [were in] Bethel and which [were] in Dan.
pieces: But Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, by which he led Israel to sin: the golden calves at Bethel and at Dan.

L.29: Only the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, which he made Israel sin, Jehu did not turn aside from after them: the calves of gold that [were in] Bethel and that [were] in Dan.

R.29: But Jehu did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat, who led Israel into sin. He did not get rid of the golden calves in the towns of Bethel and Dan.

decisions.choice: the sins of Jeroboam which he made Israel sin: the standing charge against the kings of Israel
decisions.reason: Jeroboam made two golden calves, set them at Bethel and Dan, and led Israel to worship there instead of at Jerusalem (1 Kings 12:28-30). Kings judges every king of Israel by this sin (1 Kings 16:2). Even Jehu, who wiped out Baal worship, kept the calf shrines, which held the northern kingdom apart from Judah.

decisions.choice: the golden calves at Bethel and Dan
decisions.reason: Bethel lay at the southern edge of the kingdom of Israel and Dan at its far north (1 Kings 12:29). Jeroboam presented the calves with the words "here are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of Egypt" (1 Kings 12:28), the words used of Aaron's calf (Exodus 32:4).

decisions.choice: only ... he did not turn aside from after them: the one exception
decisions.reason: "Only" sets this limit on the praise of verse 28. "From after them" pictures following the sins as one follows a leader.

decisions.choice: made Israel sin (Literal); led Israel to sin (Balanced); led Israel into sin (Readable)
decisions.reason: As at 3:3: the formula keeps one wording at each level throughout Kings.

decisions.choice: He did not get rid of
decisions.reason: Readable gives the calves a sentence of their own and names what Jehu failed to do.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֶל־יֵה֗וּא יַ֤עַן אֲשֶׁר־הֱטִיבֹ֨תָ֙ לַעֲשׂ֤וֹת הַיָּשָׁר֙ בְּעֵינַ֔י כְּכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בִּלְבָבִ֔י עָשִׂ֖יתָ לְבֵ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב בְּנֵ֣י רְבִעִ֔ים יֵשְׁב֥וּ לְךָ֖ עַל־כִּסֵּ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And said Yahweh to Jehu, because that you have done well in doing the right in my eyes, according to all that [was] in my heart you have done to [the] house of Ahab, sons of fourth [generation] will sit for you on [the] throne of Israel.
pieces: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} told Jehu, "You have done well in doing what is right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight. Because you have dealt with the house of Ahab in keeping with all that was in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart, your sons to the fourth generation will sit on the throne of Israel."

L.30: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to Jehu, "Because you have done well in doing what [is] right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes, [and] you have done to the house of Ahab according to all that [was] in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart, sons of the fourth [generation] will sit for you on the throne of Israel."

R.30: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Jehu, "You have done well. You have done what is right in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes. You have done to Ahab's family all that I wanted done. So your sons and their sons after them will rule Israel for four generations."

decisions.choice: right in my eyes: right in my judgment
decisions.reason: "In my eyes" means as Yahweh sees and judges it. The same phrase is used of the good kings of Judah (1 Kings 15:5, 11).

decisions.choice: all that was in my heart: all that I intended
decisions.reason: The heart is the seat of purpose. Jehu carried out what Yahweh had purposed against Ahab's house (1 Kings 21:21-24).

decisions.choice: sons of the fourth generation: four generations of descendants
decisions.reason: The fourth generation counts from Jehu's son: Jehoahaz, Jehoash, Jeroboam II and Zechariah all reigned after him. 15:12 records that the promise came true. Jehu's dynasty lasted longer than any other in the northern kingdom.

decisions.choice: you have done well: praise for the deed, not for every part of it
decisions.reason: Yahweh approves the removal of Ahab's house as his own judgment. Verses 29 and 31 limit the praise, and Hosea 1:4 later announces judgment on Jehu's house for the blood shed at Jezreel.

decisions.choice: your sons and their sons after them ... for four generations
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "sons of the fourth generation" means (m3).

records.heading: The rest of Jehu's reign

records.source: וְיֵה֗וּא לֹ֥א שָׁמַ֛ר לָלֶ֛כֶת בְּתֽוֹרַת־יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּכָל־לְבָב֑וֹ לֹ֣א סָ֗ר מֵעַל֙ חַטֹּ֣אות יָֽרָבְעָ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֥ר הֶחֱטִ֖יא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And Jehu not took care to walk in [the] law of Yahweh [the] God of Israel with all his heart; not he turned aside from upon [the] sins of Jeroboam which he made sin Israel.
pieces: Yet Jehu took no care to walk in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, with his whole heart. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, by which he led Israel to sin.

L.31: But Jehu did not take care to walk in the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} the God of Israel with all his heart. He did not turn aside from the sins of Jeroboam, which he made Israel sin.

R.31: But Jehu was not careful to obey the laws of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, with his whole heart. He did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam, who led Israel into sin.

decisions.choice: the law of Yahweh: his teaching and commands
decisions.reason: The word means instruction, the whole of what Yahweh taught Israel through Moses (Deuteronomy 1:5). To "walk in" it is to live by it.

decisions.choice: not with all his heart: Jehu's zeal was not wholehearted devotion
decisions.reason: Loving and obeying Yahweh "with all the heart" is the demand of Deuteronomy 6:5 and the mark of David (1 Kings 14:8). Jehu's zeal against Baal (verse 16) did not become full obedience.

decisions.choice: made Israel sin / led Israel to sin / led Israel into sin
decisions.reason: As in verse 29.

decisions.choice: the laws
decisions.reason: Readable says "laws" for the law of Yahweh, as in Deuteronomy.

records.source: בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם הֵחֵ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה לְקַצּ֖וֹת בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיַּכֵּ֥ם חֲזָאֵ֖ל בְּכָל־גְּב֥וּל יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: In the days those began Yahweh to cut off in Israel; and struck them Hazael in all [the] territory of Israel,
pieces: In those days {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} began to cut away parts of Israel. Hazael defeated the Israelites throughout their territory,

L.32: In those days {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} began to cut off [parts] of Israel, and Hazael struck them down in all the territory of Israel,

R.32: At that time {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} began to make Israel's land smaller. Hazael king of Aram defeated the Israelites all along their borders.

decisions.choice: to cut off: to cut away pieces, to make smaller
decisions.reason: The verb means to cut off the ends of something, to trim. Yahweh begins to reduce Israel's land, the first loss of the land since the conquest. Kings presents it as Yahweh's doing, in answer to the sins of verse 31.

decisions.choice: Hazael: the king of Aram whom Elisha had foreseen
decisions.reason: Elisha wept when he foresaw the harm Hazael would do to Israel (8:12), and Yahweh had named him with Jehu as an agent of judgment (1 Kings 19:15-17).

decisions.choice: in all the territory of Israel: along all Israel's borders
decisions.reason: The word means border or territory. The next verse says which regions were lost. The sentence runs on into verse 33.

decisions.choice: king of Aram
decisions.reason: Readable reminds readers who Hazael was (8:13-15).

records.source: מִן־הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִזְרַ֣ח הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ אֵ֚ת כָּל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַגִּלְעָ֔ד הַגָּדִ֥י וְהָרֻאובֵנִ֖י וְהַֽמְנַשִּׁ֑י מֵעֲרֹעֵר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־נַ֣חַל אַרְנֹ֔ן וְהַגִּלְעָ֖ד וְהַבָּשָֽׁן׃
records.gloss: from the Jordan [toward the] rising of the sun, all [the] land of the Gilead, the Gadite and the Reubenite and the Manassite, from Aroer which [is] by [the] wadi of Arnon, and the Gilead and the Bashan.
pieces: from the Jordan eastward: all the land of Gilead, the land of the Gadites, the Reubenites and the Manassites, from Aroer by the Arnon Valley, both Gilead and Bashan.

L.33: from the Jordan toward the rising of the sun, all the land of Gilead, the Gadites and the Reubenites and the Manassites, from Aroer, which [is] by the Wadi Arnon, both Gilead and Bashan.

R.33: He took all the land east of the Jordan River. This was the region of Gilead, where the tribes of Gad, Reuben and Manasseh lived. It reached from the town of Aroer by the Arnon River valley north through Gilead and Bashan.

decisions.choice: east of the Jordan: the land of the tribes of Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh
decisions.reason: These tribes had settled east of the Jordan in Moses' day (Numbers 32:33; Joshua 13:8-12). Aroer on the Arnon gorge was the southern limit of Israel's land there; Bashan lay to the north, east of the Sea of Galilee.

decisions.choice: toward the rising of the sun: eastward
decisions.reason: The east is the direction of sunrise.

decisions.choice: and Gilead and Bashan: summing up the whole region
decisions.reason: "Gilead" first names the whole land east of the Jordan; at the end, "Gilead and Bashan" names its two parts, from Aroer in the south to Bashan in the north.

decisions.choice: He took all the land
decisions.reason: Readable makes the list its own sentences and says that Hazael took these lands.

records.source: וְיֶ֨תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יֵה֛וּא וְכָל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר עָשָׂ֖ה וְכָל־גְּבוּרָת֑וֹ הֲלֽוֹא־הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of [the] matters of Jehu and all that he did and all his might, [are] not they written on [the] book of [the] matters of the days of [the] kings of Israel?
pieces: The rest of the acts of Jehu, all that he did and all his might, are written in the Book of the History of the Kings of Israel.

L.34: And the rest of the matters of Jehu, and all that he did, and all his might, are they not written in the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel?

R.34: Everything else Jehu did, and all his great deeds, is written in the history of the kings of Israel.

decisions.choice: the book of the matters of the days of the kings of Israel: the royal record named in 1 Kings 14:19
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 16:5. The question "are they not written?" means that they are.

decisions.choice: his might: his deeds of power
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 16:5. Jehu's might was shown chiefly in the bloody seizing of the throne told in chapters 9-10.

records.gloss: And lay down Jehu with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and reigned Jehoahaz his son in his place.
pieces: Jehu rested with his ancestors and was buried in Samaria, and his son Jehoahaz became king in his place.

L.35: And Jehu lay down with his fathers, and they buried him in Samaria, and Jehoahaz his son reigned in his place.

R.35: Jehu died and was buried in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz became king after him.

decisions.choice: lay down with his fathers: died
decisions.reason: The formula Kings uses for a king's death (1 Kings 16:6). Jehu, who killed two kings, himself dies in peace.

decisions.choice: the death formula
decisions.reason: As at 1 Kings 16:6: lay down with his fathers / rested with his ancestors / died.

records.gloss: And the days that reigned Jehu over Israel [were] twenty and eight year in Samaria.
pieces: Jehu reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty-eight years.

L.36: And the days that Jehu reigned over Israel [were] twenty-eight years in Samaria.

R.36: Jehu was king of Israel for twenty-eight years. He ruled from the city of Samaria.

decisions.choice: twenty-eight years: the length of Jehu's reign
decisions.reason: The usual closing note on a reign's length comes here at the end, since Jehu's reign began without the opening formula. Jehu's reign is generally dated to the second half of the ninth century BC; an Assyrian inscription, the Black Obelisk of Shalmaneser III, shows him paying tribute to Assyria.

decisions.choice: years
decisions.reason: Hebrew uses the singular "year" after numbers above ten; English needs the plural.
